summary: Round 2. Every round-1 fix was verified by mutation, not by reading: (1) MAJOR 'dead type guard' — RESOLVED and now load-bearing: replacing `getattr(exc, 'status_code', None)` with `exc.status_code` fails test_missing_status_code (AttributeError), so the rewritten test kills a real mutant where the old one killed none. (2) MAJOR 'gemini violates the shared rule' — RESOLVED, and the fix is genuinely pinned: reverting the flipped default fails test_other_client_codes_are_per_article + test_bad_request_400_is_per_article (4 failures), dropping the account set from _CLIENT_OUTAGE_CODES fails test_account_level_codes_are_outage (3), dropping 404 fails test_model_not_found_404_is_outage. All three new gemini tests earn their place. (3) MINOR 'openai tests bypass the client path' — RESOLVED; both now drive transcreate_via_claude and both die on the shared-set mutation (I confirmed dropping 407 from _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES now fails 5 places: _llm_common, claude[407], openai subtest, openrouter subtest, gemini subtest). (4) MINOR 'per-code repetition' — I withdraw it for gemini and accept the author's decision for the rest: dropping 407/408 from gemini's own _CLIENT_OUTAGE_CODES (a mutation that only exists because gemini now owns a local set) is killed ONLY by gemini's per-code loop, so that repetition is no longer redundant; for claude/openai/openrouter it stays redundant but costs two parametrize entries — not worth re-filing. (5) CAVEAT about HTTP-200-with-error-body — the reasoning is SOUND, with one refinement and one residue, see finding 6. New test_hold_logs_the_cause: verified sole killer across the FULL suite (dropping the cause from the log line fails exactly 1 of 1643 tests, that one). Answering Q2 directly: it is NOT over-coupled to wording — I rewrote the whole sentence ('article held for {link} — the LLM is unavailable (…); the next slot retries it') and all 87 tests in the hold/fallback/job/token-leak set stayed green; it is mildly over-coupled to a constant (see finding 3). Answering Q3: no previously TESTED gemini behaviour lost coverage (429/401/400/500 still pass) and the 'code missing' case is unreachable with the real SDK (APIError.__init__ always sets .code from the HTTP status), but the flip silently moved the whole unlisted-4xx band, and 409 is now the one code where the engines disagree with nothing pinning it (finding 2). Two real gaps remain in what was added this round: the gemini tests are built on an exception double that cannot exist in production (major), and the 'cause survives to the journal' contract is pinned at the log hop only — the engine hop that builds the cause string can be emptied with all 1643 tests green (finding 4). Baseline re-verified before and after every mutation: 1643 passed, 456 subtests; working tree restored (git diff empty).

findings.location: tests/test_gemini_transcreation.py:64 (_make_client_error, used by all three new gemini tests)
findings.issue: The gemini test double grants the exception an attribute the real SDK never sets, and that hides the one regression that matters. `_make_client_error` builds the error with `ClientError.__new__` and then sets BOTH `err.code` and `err.status_code`. Verified against the installed google-genai 1.73.1: `APIError.__init__` sets only `.response`, `.details`, `.message`, `.status`, `.code` — a genuine `ClientError(402, {...}, None)` has `hasattr(exc, 'status_code') == False` (checked by construction; the real object classifies correctly, so the implementation is right today). Mutation proof: changing the classifier line to `code = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)` (i.e. dropping the `.code` read that is the only one that works in production) leaves the gemini file fully green — 35 passed, 6 subtests passed. In production that mutation makes `code` None for EVERY 4xx, so a real 402 falls straight through the new per-article default and strikes the article out — precisely the 2026-07-14 loss this change exists to prevent. The whole newly-rewritten gemini branch is therefore pinned only against a shape that cannot occur, which is exactly the fidelity problem round 1 fixed in the openai/openrouter files (they now build real `openai.APIStatusError` through httpx) and gemini did not.

Answer to 'does the flipped default leave previously-covered behaviour untested': no previously TESTED case regressed (429/401/400/500 all still pass, and the unparseable-code case is unreachable — `APIError.raise_error` always passes the HTTP status into `APIError.__init__`, so `.code` is always an int), but the flip moved every unlisted 4xx from outage to per-article in one step and 409 is the code where that now contradicts the sibling engines. openai_transcreation.py:239 and openrouter_transcreation.py:331 both list `openai.ConflictError` (409) on the OUTAGE side; gemini now classifies 409 as per-article. Mutation proof that nothing pins it: adding 409 to `_CLIENT_OUTAGE_CODES` leaves the gemini file green (35 passed, 6 subtests), and grep shows no test in the repo asserts 409 for any engine. The new test's docstring ('matching the other three engines') is therefore only two-thirds true — it matches claude (which does not list `anthropic.ConflictError`, so 409 falls to its per-article default) and contradicts openai/openrouter.
findings.recommendation: Pick a side and pin it. If 409 is account-level (it is a lock/conflict on the API resource, not on the article text — which is why the two openai-based engines hold it), add it to the shared decision: `_CLIENT_OUTAGE_CODES = frozenset({401, 403, 404, 409, 429}) | _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES`, add `anthropic.ConflictError` to claude_transcreation's outage tuple, and extend the existing loops — `for code in (402, 407, 408, 409)` in test_account_level_codes_are_outage and a `test_conflict_409_is_outage` in test_claude_transcreation.py mirroring test_account_level_status_raises_outage. If 409 is meant to stay per-article for gemini, keep the code as is but fix the docstring to 'matching claude; openai/openrouter additionally hold 409 via ConflictError' and add `409` to the `for code in (413, 414, 451)` loop so the choice is asserted rather than incidental.

findings.issue: Direct answer to the over-coupling question, with mutations. Wording: NOT over-coupled — I replaced the entire sentence with a different phrasing that keeps only the type name and the sanitized message, and all 87 tests in the hold/fallback/job/token-leak selection stayed green. But one of the three assertions pins a constant: at `except ClaudeOutageError as exc:` the value of `type(exc).__name__` is always the string 'ClaudeOutageError' (no subclass of it exists in the repo), so that assertion carries zero diagnostic information — it cannot distinguish an empty balance from a dead network, which is the stated purpose of the test — yet it fails a harmless simplification: dropping the redundant class name while keeping the cause (`f"[hold] LLM outage for {link}: {sanitize_error_message(exc)} — …"`) kills the test even though the operator loses nothing. Meanwhile the one property of that interpolation actually worth pinning is unpinned: swapping `sanitize_error_message(exc)` for a bare `{exc}` leaves all 87 tests green, including the whole of tests/test_no_token_leak_in_logs.py (grep confirms that file never exercises the hold path). Live-leak risk is low because `_TokenRedactingFilter` on the root logger scrubs key SHAPES, but it does not cover the non-key secrets `sanitize_error_message` handles (TELEGRAM_CHANNEL_ID / TELEGRAM_ADMIN_ID / TELEGRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN, news_bot.py:229), so the redaction on this brand-new interpolation is genuinely untested.
findings.recommendation: Spend the third assertion on the sanitizer instead of on a constant. Keep `assertIn('402', ...)` and `assertIn('Insufficient credits', ...)`; replace `assertIn('ClaudeOutageError', ...)` with a redaction pin — wrap the call in `with patch.dict(os.environ, {'TELEGRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN': '<FAKE-TOKEN-ELIDED>'}):`, raise `ClaudeOutageError('APIStatusError: 402 Insufficient credits (token tgph-sentinel-9f3c)')`, then assert `self.assertNotIn('tgph-sentinel-9f3c', hold_lines[0])` and `self.assertIn('[REDACTED]', hold_lines[0])`. That sentinel is matched by `_SECRET_ENV_NAMES` but by none of the `_redact_text` key regexes, so it fails iff the line stops going through `sanitize_error_message` — the mutation that currently survives. Keep `assertEqual(len(hold_lines), 1)` as is.

findings.issue: The 'cause reaches the journal' contract is pinned at one hop out of two, so it can still be broken with a green suite. test_hold_logs_the_cause proves news_bot interpolates whatever string the exception carries, but the string is hand-written by the test (`ClaudeOutageError('APIStatusError: 402 Insufficient credits')`); no test asserts that the engines put the cause INTO it. Every engine test asserts only the exception TYPE. Mutation proof on the engine that actually runs in production: replacing the account-level branch's `return ClaudeOutageError(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")` with `return ClaudeOutageError("LLM outage")` in openrouter_transcreation passes the ENTIRE suite — 1643 passed, 456 subtests. After that mutation the journal line reads '[hold] LLM outage for <link>: ClaudeOutageError: LLM outage', the operator is back to being unable to tell an empty balance from a dead network, and the change's own documented invariant (patterns.md: 'the cause of a hold exists ONLY in the [hold] log line') is silently void. For reference, the real production string is worth preserving: a genuine OpenRouter 402 gives `str(exc) == "Error code: 402 - {'error': {'message': 'Insufficient credits…', 'code': 402}}"` (verified via `client._make_status_error_from_response`), so both the number and the text do survive today.
findings.recommendation:
One assertion in the test that already exists. In test_payment_required_is_outage, capture and inspect the exception instead of only its type:

    with patch.object(openrouter_transcreation, "_load_prompt", return_value="X"):
        with self.assertRaises(ClaudeOutageError) as ctx:
            openrouter_transcreation.transcreate_via_claude(SAMPLE_ARTICLE, client=client)
    self.assertIn("Insufficient credits", str(ctx.exception))
    self.assertIn("402", str(ctx.exception))

For the '402' half to hold, make the helper message SDK-shaped so the double stops being weaker than production: in `_make_status_error`, default `message` to `f"Error code: {status_code} - {{'error': {{'message': {message!r}, 'code': {status_code}}}}}"`, or simply call it as `_make_status_error(402, "Error code: 402 - {'error': {'message': 'Insufficient credits', 'code': 402}}")`. Verify by re-running the mutation above: it must then fail this test. Mirror the same two assertions in test_claude_transcreation.py::test_account_level_status_raises_outage[402] if you want the invariant covered per engine; one engine is enough to kill the mutant class.

findings.location: openrouter_transcreation.py:451-458 (response-shape branch) + tests/test_openrouter_transcreation.py — round-1 finding 4, status: caveat resolved, coverage gap still open
findings.issue: Your reasoning about the wire format is sound, and I checked it rather than accepting it. The stored value is written as `f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"`, so the literal token 'APIStatusError' in the record can only come from an object whose class name IS 'APIStatusError' — the bare class, not a subclass (a subclass would render its own name). The openai SDK instantiates the bare `APIStatusError` in exactly one place, `_make_status_error_from_response`, reached only when `not response.is_success`; I reproduced it (`httpx.Response(402, json={'error': {'message': 'Insufficient credits', 'code': 402}})` → type APIStatusError, `.status_code == 402`). The 200-with-bad-body alternative cannot produce that name: it raises `APIResponseValidationError`, whose MRO is (APIResponseValidationError, APIError, OpenAIError) — NOT an APIStatusError — so it already falls to the `openai.APIError` catch-all and is classified as an OUTAGE anyway. Two honest residues. (a) The evidence is a human-written session note, not the DB row: work/SESSION-2026-08-03.md:220 and PLAN-2026-08-03.md:21 both paraphrase ('APIStatusError 402 Insufficient credits'; the verbatim last_error would read 'APIStatusError: Error code: 402 - {...}'), and the local news.db has no tables, so I could not re-verify against data. (b) The one shape that is neither of the above is still uncovered and I confirmed it is reachable: OpenRouter's documented 200 + in-body error object parses leniently (`construct_type(value={'error': {...}}, type_=ChatCompletion)` returns a ChatCompletion with `choices = None`), so `response.choices[0]` raises TypeError → the `except (AttributeError, IndexError, TypeError)` handler at openrouter_transcreation.py:452 → ClaudeTranscreationError → per-article strike, with the 402 sitting untouched in `response.error`. grep for 'response shape unexpected' and 'content is empty' across tests/ still returns zero hits.
findings.recommendation: Close the 402 half — the record supports it and the alternative path is already held. Keep two small items: (1) add the missing branch test regardless of the 402 question, in TestExceptionClassification: `resp = MagicMock(); resp.choices = None; client = _make_client_returning(resp)`, then `with self.assertRaises(ClaudeTranscreationError) as ctx: …` and `self.assertIn('response shape unexpected', str(ctx.exception))` — that error path is wholly untested today. (2) If you want the in-body case held rather than struck, add a pre-parse guard before reading choices: `err = getattr(response, 'error', None)` and, when `isinstance(err, dict) and err.get('code') in _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES`, `raise ClaudeOutageError(f"OpenRouter in-body error {err.get('code')}: {err.get('message')}")`, with a test building `resp.error = {'code': 402, 'message': 'Insufficient credits'}` and `resp.choices = None`. Optional — the incident record points at a real HTTP 402, so this is belt-and-braces.

findings.location: tests/test_job_distributed_publish.py:508 (test_outage_active_routes_via_google) — round-1 finding 6, status: not applied, unchanged
findings.issue: Still stale after round 2. The name says 'routes via google' and the docstring still asserts '_fallback_publish itself short-circuits to Google internally on the active-fallback flag', but that behaviour was removed by the 2026-06-11 hold-and-wait decision, and tests/test_llm_outage_hold.py:139 pins the opposite with mock_google wired to raise if called. Assertions are correct so nothing fails; the file simply documents forbidden behaviour in the exact area this change touches, and this round adds a second test (test_hold_logs_the_cause) to the file that contradicts it.
findings.recommendation: Rename to test_fallback_active_still_routes_through_fallback_publish and rewrite the docstring to the current contract: 'is_fallback_active() == True must not skip the slot — the loop still calls _fallback_publish so the LLM is retried and a recovery can be detected; there is no Google short-circuit (see tests/test_llm_outage_hold.py::test_fallback_active_does_not_route_to_google).' Assertions stay as they are.
